source.title: Taxonomizing local versus global structure in neural network loss landscapes
source.authors: Yaoqing Yang; Liam Hodgkinson; Ryan Theisen; Joe Zou; Joseph E. Gonzalez; K. Ramchandran; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model width, batch size, and label noise and reports training-loss outcomes, but it does not directly report the training classification-error results specified by the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss and mode-connectivity results for ResNet18 on CIFAR-10, including with 10% randomized labels. These are related to fitting the training data, but the reported outcomes do not directly establish training classification error. The plotted loss values are not transcribed as exact numbers here.
record.test_reason: The study trains convolutional networks from random initialization with SGD on CIFAR-10, varying width and label corruption. Nearly zero cross-entropy training loss establishes nearly zero classification error, and Figure 12 additionally reports training classification error directly. The record incorrectly excludes these results solely because they report loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors principally conclude that best test performance coincides with globally well-connected landscapes, similar trained representations and locally flat solutions; local sharpness alone is insufficient. They also find that nearly zero training loss can worsen test performance in some poorly connected settings, with insufficient exploration offered as an explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies loss-landscape structure across width, batch size, data quantity and quality; it does not reproduce the original training-error studies or directly report their target measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with model width, batch size or learning rate, label noise, data quantity, and learning-rate decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width improves mode connectivity, while additional data improves representation similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width and data quantity affect distinct global properties of trained neural-network loss landscapes.

fits_no_version.finding: In some poorly connected settings, fitting to nearly zero training loss gives worse test performance than configurations with higher training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of fitting training data depends on landscape connectivity and training conditions.

record.problems: The reported text describes training loss rather than training classification error for the relevant results; several outcomes are presented in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Other figures report loss-landscape metrics, test accuracy, or other datasets and do not directly establish the versions’ stated training-classification-error outcome.

untested.parts: Fully randomized labels, Adam, and systematic early-stopping or regularization comparisons are not established by the linked results. CIFAR-100 appears in Figure 15, but the supplied text does not establish its endpoint training-error rates.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or comparison with one or two extra student neurons.
No controlled depth comparison or shortcut ablation.
No comparison of initialization schemes, signal propagation or trainable depth.
No loss-and-curvature training trajectories relative to the initial stability threshold. Varying learning rate and measuring final sharpness does not test this version.
No batch-normalization ablation or Fixup comparison.

missing.what: Original-label CIFAR-10 training-loss results: Appendix A.4.1 explicitly identifies Phases III/IV as attaining nearly zero training loss. Extract these separately from the corrupted-label results.

Direct training classification-error curves, including the fixed trained endpoints. The caption identifies nearly zero error in bottom-right configurations and insufficiently trained endpoints in top-right configurations. Extract endpoint errors by width and batch size; the optimized interior curve points are not independent standard-training outcomes.
missing.locator: Appendix A.5, Figure 12; Section 2 specifies 0–1 loss for mode connectivity

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Higher nonzero cross-entropy alone does not establish substantial classification error, and poor mode connectivity alone does not establish convergence to a spurious local minimum.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports training loss, not training classification error; it does not directly establish the version’s classification-error claim, including its CIFAR-100 and random-label conditions.

rows.value: Phase III and Phase IV achieve almost exactly zero loss; Phase I and Phase II do not.
rows.note: The text describes loss, not classification error; the version requires training classification error.
rows.check: The nearly zero training loss in Phases III/IV bears on V1: for ordinary cross-entropy, classification error is bounded above by mean loss divided by ln(2). This is an inference from the reported loss, not a directly transcribed error rate. Split the row by phase: nonzero loss in Phases I/II alone cannot establish substantial classification error. Labels were changed to incorrect classes for 10% of samples; training used random initialization, SGD, constant learning rate and no augmentation.
